title: Chromosome Analysis and Sorting Using Conventional Flow Cytometers
protocol: Culture cells in T-75 cm² flasks with 50 ml RPMI 1640 cell culture medium at 37°C in a 5% CO₂ incubator.
Remove half of the spent culture medium when it turns yellow without disturbing the cell clusters.
Subculture near-confluent cells at a ratio of 1:1 in two flasks.
Bring the volume in each flask to 50 ml with fresh culture medium.
Incubate the flasks at 37°C in a 5% CO2 incubator.
Add colcemid to a final concentration of 0.1 μg/ml after 24 hours.
Gently swirl the flask to mix well.
Incubate for 6 hr.
Incubate cells with mitotic inhibitors to achieve a high mitotic index.
Optimize treatment time for each cell type based on the rate of cell growth.
Collect cells suspended in the supernatant from both flasks.
Transfer collected cells to two 50-ml polypropylene centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge at 289 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Carefully remove the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.
Invert the tube on an absorbent paper and drain excess medium.
Culture cells in T-150 cm² flasks with 25 ml DMEM at 37°C in a 5% CO₂ incubator.
When the culture is near-confluent (∼75% surface coverage), remove the spent medium.
Briefly rinse the cell layer with 5 ml sterile 1× PBS and then discard the buffer using a sterile 10-ml pipette.
Add 3 ml TrypLE Express and ensure it covers the entire surface of the flask.
Incubate at 37°C for 3-5 min.
Tap the bottom of the flask gently to detach all of the cells.
Add 5 ml fresh culture medium and mix well to obtain a single-cell suspension.
Subculture the cell suspension at a ratio of 1:3 in four flasks.
Bring the volume to 25 ml with fresh culture medium.
Incubate at 37°C in a 5% CO₂ incubator.
Add colcemid to the flask to a final concentration of 0.1 µg/ml and gently swirl to mix well.
Incubate for 6-16 hr after adding colcemid.
Gently tap the bottom of the flasks to dislodge cells at metaphase.
Collect cells suspended in the supernatant from four flasks and transfer them to two 50-ml polypropylene centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge collected cells at 289 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Remove the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.
Invert the tube on absorbent paper and drain the excess medium.
Proceed to Basic Protocol 2.
Treat harvested colcemid-treated cells with hypotonic solution.
Mechanically disrupt treated cells after swelling and spreading of chromosomes within the plasma membrane.
Disrupt mechanically disrupted cells further using a modified polyamine isolation buffer (PAB).
Stain the released chromosomes with Turck's stain.
Add propidium iodide at a concentration of 1 mg/ml for staining.
Transfer samples to a 50-ml polypropylene centrifuge tube.
Move stained samples into a 15-ml polypropylene centrifuge tube.
Place samples in a 5-ml BD Falcon tube.
Filter the samples through a 20-µm mesh filter.
Use a 2 ml Pasteur pipette for sample handling.
Vortex the mixture to mix thoroughly.
Resuspend the cell pellets from Basic Protocol 1 in hypotonic solution (∼5 ml per tube) with a Pasteur pipette.
Combine the cell suspensions in a single 50-ml polypropylene centrifuge tube.
Incubate the combined cell suspension at room temperature for about 15 min.
Mix 5 µl of cell suspension with 5 µl of Turck's stain on a microscope slide.
Monitor cells under a light microscope for swelling if using Turck's stain.
Alternatively, use 1 mg/ml PI and view under a fluorescence microscope to assess cell swelling.
Assess the cells for chromosome spread within the plasma membrane.
Incubate for an additional 10 to 30 min if needed to achieve optimal cell swelling.
Centrifuge swollen cells at 289 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Remove the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.
Invert the tube on absorbent paper and drain excess medium.
Add 1 to 2 ml of ice-cold PAB to the cell pellet.
Gently resuspend using a Pasteur pipette.
Incubate on ice for 10 min.
Disrupt the cells by vortexing for 10-20 seconds.
Stain 5 μl of cell suspension with 5 μl PI on a microscope slide.
Gently cover the stained suspension with a coverslip.
View the stained chromosome suspension under the fluorescence microscope.
Check for single intact chromosomes.
Vortex as needed if numerous chromosome clumps are observed in the stained suspension.
Alternatively, draw up and expel the suspension several times using a 5-ml syringe attached to a 22.5 G needle.
Transfer the chromosome suspension to a 15-ml polypropylene centrifuge tube.
Spin at 201 × g for 2 minutes at room temperature.
Collect the supernatant in a 5-ml Falcon tube after filtering through a 20-μm mesh filter.
Per 1 ml chromosome suspension, stain overnight with 5 μl of 1 mg/ml DAPI (final concentration 5 μg/ml).
Per 1 ml chromosome suspension, stain overnight with 5 μl of 1 mg/ml PI (final concentration 5 μg/ml).
Per 1 ml chromosome suspension, add 10 μl of 1 M MgSO4·7H2O (final concentration 10 mM).
Per 1 ml chromosome suspension, add 10 μl sodium citrate (final concentration 10 mM).
Per 1 ml chromosome suspension, add 50 μl of 500 mM sodium sulfite (final concentration 25 mM).
Store the stained chromosomes in the dark at 4°C overnight before flow analysis and sorting.
For 1 ml chromosome suspension, stain overnight with 5 μl of 1 mg/ml HO (final concentration 5 µg/ml).
Add 5 μl of 10 mg/ml CA3 (final concentration 50 µg/ml) for staining.
Add 10 μl of 1 M MgSO4·7H2O (final concentration 10 mM) to the suspension.
Add 10 μl sodium citrate (final concentration 10 mM) to the suspension.
Add 50 μl of 500 mM sodium sulfite (final concentration 25 mM) to the suspension.
Store the stained chromosome suspension in the dark at 4°C overnight before flow analysis and sorting.
Briefly vortex the stained chromosome sample for 5 s.
Centrifuge the chromosome suspension at 201 × g for 3 min at 4°C.
Filter supernatant through a 20-µm mesh into a 5-ml BD Falcon tube.
Store the filtered sample on ice.
Perform daily maintenance on the BD LSR Fortessa according to manufacturer instructions.
Vortex BD CST beads thoroughly for 5 seconds.
Mix 2 drops of beads with 500 µl cell staining buffer in a 5-ml Falcon tube.
Verify that the cytometer performance check has passed before proceeding to experiment set-up.
Set up the instrument for chromosome analysis using the specified parameters.
For DAPI detection, select the 450/50 (355) filter and set signal detection to Area and Width.
For PI detection using the 561 nm laser, select the 610/20 (561) filter and set signal detection to Area and Width.
Label parameters as shown in Figure 4B.
Set the Threshold level at 10,000 for 450/50 (355).
Create dot plots for DAPI 450_50 (355)-A versus DAPI 450_50 (355)-W.
Create dot plots for DAPI 450_50 (355)-A versus PI 610_20 (561)-A.
Create dot plots for DAPI 450_50 (355)-A versus PI LP620 710_50 (488)-A.
Adjust the RUN to a data rate of 1000 events per second.
Adjust the voltage for both detectors with chromosome clusters displayed along a 45° angle.
Draw a region gate R1 on plot DAPI 450_50 (355)-A versus DAPI 450_50 (355)-W to gate out debris and clumps.
Display gated events R1 on DAPI 450_50 (355)-A versus PI 610_20 (561)-A.
Display gated events R1 on DAPI 450_50 (355)-A versus PI LP620 710_50 (488)-A.
Acquire and save 50,000 to 100,000 events.
Analyse and compare collected chromosome data to the data from Figure 17A.
Verify if most chromosome clusters can be identified.
Briefly vortex the stained chromosome sample for 5 seconds.
Centrifuge the chromosome suspension at 201 × g for 3 minutes at 4°C.
Filter supernatant through a 20-µm mesh into a 5 ml tube.
Store the filtered sample on ice.
Replace the sheath tank with chromosome sheath buffer.
Set the sheath pressure to 60 PSI.
Install a clean 70 µm nozzle.
Perform daily maintenance on the cell sorter as directed.
Perform instrument laser alignment and drop delay calibration using Bigfoot calibration beads according to manufacturer instructions.
Verify that the sorter passed daily QC and the drop delay is established before proceeding to experimental setup.
Select ‘Quick Run’ and select the parameters used for the chromosome analysis experiment.
In Flex Controls, select ‘Detection’ and relabel the selected parameters.
For DAPI detection, within 349 nm parameters select band-pass BP 455/14.
Under ‘Optical Filters’, replace BP 455/14 with a long-pass LP 420 filter.
For PI detection, within 561 nm parameters select band-pass BP 625/15.
Under ‘Optical Filters’, replace BP 625/15 with a long-pass LP 570 filter.
Select 2D Trigger ‘ON’ and 2D Trigger mode ‘AND’ in the Control Panel.
Optimize the level for both parameters selected for 349 nm and 561 nm or 488 nm.
Create a single parameter histogram plot for 349 nm-DAPI LP420, 561 nm-PI LP570, and 488 nm-PI 614/24.
Align lasers with minimum CVs for the DAPI and PI fluorescence channels using the Nozzle Mover Panel control.
Run a tube containing Bigfoot calibration beads at a flow rate of 250 events/s.
Create dot plots for (A) 349 nm-DAPI LP420 (Area Linear) versus 349 nm-DAPI LP420 (Width Linear).
Create dot plots for (B) 349 nm-DAPI LP420 Area Linear versus 561 nm-PI LP570 Area Linear.
Optimize the RUN with a flow rate of 1000-1500 events per second.
Draw a region gate on plot 349 nm-DAPI LP420 (Area –Linear) versus 349 nm-DAPI LP420 (Width-Linear).
Display gated events in R1 on 349 nm-DAPI LP420 (Area-Linear) versus 561 nm-PI LP570 (Area-Linear).
Adjust the voltage until chromosome clusters are displayed along a 45° angle.
Acquire and save 50,000 to 100,000 events.
Analyze and compare the collected chromosome data to reference data.
Draw the region gate around the chromosome cluster of interest for sorting.
Draw a region gate around chromosomes Y, 13, 17, and 19.
Select ‘Tube1-5ml’ sort media option for sorting into 1.5-ml Eppendorf tubes.
Calibrate and adjust the test sort stream to align with the collection tube.
Set Sort Mode to Purity.
Specify the required number of chromosomes to be sorted per Eppendorf tube.
Position the empty 1.5-ml Eppendorf tubes in the sorting collection area.
Run the chromosome sample for a couple of minutes or until clusters stabilize.
Reposition the sort gate on selected chromosome clusters if necessary.
Proceed with the sorting process.
Store the flow-sorted chromosomes at 4°C.
Handle the Eppendorf tubes containing flow-sorted material gently.
Add 15 µl SARC/EDTA and 2.5 µl proteinase K to each tube.
Incubate overnight at 42°C.
Dilute 20 mg/ml PMSF to 4 mg/ml with absolute ethanol.
Add 2 μl of the diluted PMSF to each sorted DNA tube.
Incubate for 40 min at room temperature.
Add 10 μl of 5 M NaCl (final concentration of 0.3 M including sheath buffer) to the tubes.
Add 2 μl of pellet paint and 770 μl of absolute ethanol to each tube.
Mix gently by inversion.
Store overnight at −20°C.
Pellet the sorted chromosomes at 15,700 × g for 15 min at room temperature.
Remove most of the supernatant with a P1000 pipette tip.
Remove any remaining solution with a P200 pipette tip without disturbing the pellet.
Add 1 ml of 70% (v/v) ethanol to each tube without disturbing the pellet.
Centrifuge again for 7 min at 15,700 × g, room temperature.
Remove the supernatant as in step 6.
Repeat the 70% ethanol wash one more time and allow the pellets to air-dry at RT for 10 min.
Resuspend the pellet in 100 μl sterile Tris-EDTA buffer.
Proceed to genomics assays, i.e., sequencing or microarray experiments.
